recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Schema + model + repository: reverses_request_id
recommended_phases.rationale: Add the nullable self-referencing column first so every later layer has a real field to carry. New knex migration `migrations/<ts>_add_reverses_request_id_to_leave_requests.js` (alterTable add `t.string('reverses_request_id').references('id').inTable('leave_requests')` + `t.index(['reverses_request_id'])`; down drops index then column). Then `leave.model.ts` gains `reversesRequestId: string | null` (CreateLeaveRequestInput follows automatically via Omit), and `leave.repository.ts` threads it end-to-end: `LeaveRequestRow`, `COLUMNS`, `mapRow`, the 15-value INSERT, and a new `findByReversesRequestId(reversesRequestId, client)` for the duplicate-reversal guard. No service or route change yet, so the existing suite stays green.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — LeaveService.cancel: reversal branch for APPROVED
recommended_phases.rationale: The single behavioural change, confined to `leave.service.ts`. Split `cancel` on the loaded request's status: DRAFT/SUBMITTED keep the current in-place `repository.update(... status: CANCELLED, cancelledBy, cancelledAt ...)` path untouched; APPROVED instead calls `repository.create({ ...original fields, status: CANCELLED, reversesRequestId: request.id, cancelledBy: actor.id, cancelledAt: now, approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt copied or nulled per the open question })` and never calls `update` on the original id. The balance release (`usedDays -= request.requestedDays`) stays exactly where it is, inside the same `uow.withTransaction`, executed once, with the row locked via `resolveBalance(..., client, true)`. The CANCEL audit entry is still written, with `entityId` = the NEW row id and `beforeState` = the original APPROVED row so the immutability is provable from the audit trail. The notification is unchanged. `assertCanCancel` and the startDate timing guard are unchanged.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Read-model exposure + unit tests
recommended_phases.rationale: `reversesRequestId` reaches the wire for free once Phase 1 added it to `COLUMNS`/`mapRow`, so `GET /leaves` and `GET /leaves/:id` need no route edit — this phase verifies that and pins it. Extend `tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts`: (a) cancel APPROVED → the fake repository records ZERO `update` calls against the original id, exactly ONE `create` with `status: CANCELLED` and `reversesRequestId === original.id`, the original fixture still reads APPROVED, `usedDays` decremented by exactly `requestedDays` once, one CANCEL audit entry, one notification, all inside a single `withTransaction` callback with the stub client forwarded; (b) cancel DRAFT and cancel SUBMITTED still mutate in place and create no new row; (c) the reversal row is returned by `list`/`getById` with `reversesRequestId` populated. Update the `FakeLeaveRepository` to implement `findByReversesRequestId` and the fixtures to carry `reversesRequestId: null`.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — Smoke proof against real Postgres
recommended_phases.rationale: Extend `scripts/smoke.js` (Postgres mode) with the acceptance proof that only a real database can give: create → submit → approve a request, then cancel it, then assert via `GET /leaves/:id` that the ORIGINAL id still reads `status === 'APPROVED'` with its `approverId`/`decidedAt` intact, and that a second row exists whose `reversesRequestId` equals the original id and whose `status === 'CANCELLED'`. Assert the balance `usedDays` returned to its pre-approval value exactly once (not twice). This is the stage that catches a repository `COLUMNS`/`mapRow` omission that unit fakes cannot see.

app_notes:
## Layer boundaries (dependencies flow inward only)

- **Presentation** — `leave.routes.ts` (Fastify handlers, `resolveActor`, `parseCreateBody`, `parseQuery`, `sendError`). No controller file; routes call the service directly (established convention). Routes own wire→domain conversion (string→Date) and RBAC at the API boundary; they contain no business logic and no SQL.
- **Application** — `ILeaveService`/`LeaveService` (orchestration, authorization, transaction boundary), plus the sibling services it composes (`IBalanceService`, `IAuditService`, `INotificationService`, `IValidationService`, `IEmployeeService`, `IPolicyService`). The service owns *what* is in the transaction; it never issues BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK.
- **Domain** — models and pure rules: `LeaveRequest`, `LeaveBalance`, `AuditLog`, `Notification`, `Employee`, `LeavePolicy`, `LeaveType`, `ValidationResult`, and the shared `requestedDays` helper. No I/O.
- **Infrastructure** — `ILeaveRepository`/`PgLeaveRequestRepository`, `IBalanceRepository`/`PgLeaveBalanceRepository`, `IAuditRepository`, `INotificationRepository`, `IEmployeeRepository`, `IPolicyRepository`, `ILeaveTypeRepository`, `IUnitOfWork`/`PgUnitOfWork`, the pg Pool, and `migrations/`. This is the only layer that touches the database and the only place BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK are issued.

## Where this feature lands

The change is confined to the **leave** module plus one migration. No new module is created and no new cross-module value type is introduced: the reversal is represented by `LeaveRequest` itself gaining `reversesRequestId`, so the shared-types placement rule is satisfied by *not* adding anything to `src/shared/types/`. `reversesRequestId` is a field on an entity owned by exactly one module, so it belongs in `src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts`, not in shared types.

`cancel(actor, requestId)` branches on the loaded request's status:
- **DRAFT / SUBMITTED** — unchanged in-place `repository.update(id, { status: CANCELLED, cancelledBy, cancelledAt })`. No completed approval exists, so GP-008 does not apply.
- **APPROVED** — the original row is never written. `repository.create(...)` inserts a NEW row with `status: CANCELLED` and `reversesRequestId = request.id`. The original's `status`, `approverId`, `approvalComment` and `decidedAt` are immutable by construction because no UPDATE statement targets that id.

Balance release is unchanged and stays inside the same `uow.withTransaction`: `usedDays -= request.requestedDays` exactly once, computed from the ORIGINAL row's `requestedDays`, with the balance row locked via `resolveBalance(..., client, true)`. The CANCEL audit entry is still written (GP-002), with `entityId` = the new reversal row and `beforeState` = the original APPROVED row, so the audit trail itself proves the original was not mutated. The notification is unchanged.

## Dependency map verification (no cycles)

Edges: `leave → {balance, audit, notification, employee, policy, validation, shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db, shared-date, shared-auth}`; `balance → {employee, policy, shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db, shared-date}`; `policy → {leave-type, shared-types, shared-errors}`; `leave-type → {shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db}`; `employee → {shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db, shared-auth}`; `audit → {shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db}`; `notification → {shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db}`; `validation → {shared-types, shared-errors}`; `shared-date → {shared-errors}`; `shared-auth → {shared-types, shared-errors}`; `shared-db → {shared-errors}`.

Topological order: shared-errors → shared-types → shared-db → shared-date → shared-auth → leave-type → policy → employee → audit → notification → validation → balance → leave. Every edge points from a later module to an earlier one; no module depends back on `leave`; no cycle exists. `leave` remains the sole orchestrator. All cross-module imports go through each module's `index.ts` public entry point (AGENTS.md rule 1).

## Golden-principle compliance

- **GP-001** — the reversal insert and the balance release both go through repository interfaces; no inline SQL in the service.
- **GP-002** — the CANCEL audit record is still written for both branches.
- **GP-003** — input validation stays at the API boundary (`parseCreateBody`/`parseQuery`) and in `ValidationService`.
- **GP-005** — RBAC is enforced by `resolveActor` at the route boundary and by `assertCanCancel` in the service; never inline in a handler.
- **GP-006** — every handler wraps its call in try/catch and funnels through `sendError`.

## Transaction semantics

`IUnitOfWork.withTransaction` (PgUnitOfWork) is the only place BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK are issued. The reversal is one unit of work: insert reversal row → release balance → write audit → notify. Every participating repository/service method takes an optional trailing `PoolClient` and joins the caller's transaction. A failure anywhere rolls back the whole reversal, so the balance is never released without the reversal row existing.

open_questions.question: What field values does the NEW CANCELLED reversal row carry for the fields it does not own — specifically requestedDays, startDate/endDate/leaveTypeCode, and approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt?
open_questions.impact: The reversal row is what GET /leaves returns to the client, so these values are the wire contract. If requestedDays is copied from the original, a naive client summing requestedDays over CANCELLED rows double-counts the leave; if it is 0, the row no longer describes the span it reverses. approverId/decidedAt on the reversal row are also ambiguous: copying them makes the reversal row look like it was itself approved, while nulling them loses the link to who decided the original. The balance release amount must remain the ORIGINAL's requestedDays regardless of this choice.
candidate_options: Copy startDate/endDate/leaveTypeCode/requestedDays from the original; set approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt to null on the reversal row (the reversal was never approved)
Copy startDate/endDate/leaveTypeCode/requestedDays AND approverId/decidedAt from the original, so the reversal row is a faithful snapshot of what was reversed
Copy startDate/endDate/leaveTypeCode but set requestedDays = 0 on the reversal row, so summing requestedDays over non-CANCELLED rows stays correct

open_questions.question: May an APPROVED request be reversed more than once — i.e. is a second cancel of the same original id rejected, and how?
open_questions.impact: Without a guard, a second cancel of the same APPROVED original inserts a second CANCELLED row and releases usedDays a second time — the exact double-release the feature forbids. The guard's shape decides whether the new `findByReversesRequestId` repository method is load-bearing or dead code, and whether the failure is a 409 ConflictError (already reversed) or a silent no-op returning the existing reversal row.
candidate_options: Reject with ConflictError(409) when findByReversesRequestId(original.id) already returns a row — the reversal is a one-shot operation
Idempotent: return the existing reversal row unchanged (200) without touching the balance again
No guard — rely on the startDate timing guard alone (rejected: it does not prevent a second reversal before the leave starts)

open_questions.question: Should GET /leaves return reversal rows by default, or only when explicitly asked for?
open_questions.impact: A cancelled-after-approval request is now two rows, so an unfiltered list shows both the APPROVED original and its CANCELLED reversal for the same leave span. Clients that render a leave calendar or sum days will double-count unless they filter on reversesRequestId. The choice decides whether LeaveRequestQueryParams needs a new filter (e.g. excludeReversals / reversesRequestId) and whether the default list is a superset or a de-duplicated view.
candidate_options: Return both rows unfiltered; the client distinguishes them via reversesRequestId (matches the feature's stated requirement literally)
Return both rows but add an optional query filter so a client can request only originals or only reversals
Exclude reversal rows from the default list and expose them only via GET /leaves/:id

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: EmployeeRole } where EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'. Identity and role are obtained from a JWT bearer token verified by the existing `registerAuth` preHandler in `src/shared/auth/index.ts`, which populates `request.user` from `payload.sub` (id) and `payload.role`; the canonical `AuthUser` type lives in `src/shared/auth/`. RBAC is enforced at the API boundary by the route-level `resolveActor` helper (throws UnauthorizedError on a missing/invalid actor) and in the service by `assertCanCancel` — never inline in a handler. Cancel authorization is unchanged by this feature: the owner may cancel their own DRAFT or SUBMITTED request; only an APPROVED request may be cancelled by a non-owner, and then only by the requester's direct manager (`employee.managerId === actor.id`) or an ADMIN (exempt from the direct-manager check). All leave endpoints require a valid token; `POST /auth/login` is the only public path.
error_response_contract: Errors return { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure -> HTTP 400 (ValidationError, code 'VALIDATION'); authentication failure -> HTTP 401 (UnauthorizedError, code 'UNAUTHORIZED'); authorization failure -> HTTP 403 (ForbiddenError, code 'FORBIDDEN'); not found -> HTTP 404 (NotFoundError, code 'NOT_FOUND'); invalid state transition or a second reversal of an already-reversed request -> HTTP 409 (ConflictError, code 'CONFLICT'); any other throw -> HTTP 500 with { error: 'Internal Server Error' }. `GET /leaves/:id` returns the same 404 for a request the caller may not see as for one that does not exist. `POST /leaves/:id/cancel` returns 200 with the resulting row: the mutated original for DRAFT/SUBMITTED, or the NEW CANCELLED reversal row (carrying reversesRequestId) for APPROVED.
